gets an Activity-level pause. Native, by contrast, re-inflates a fresh
Fragment per order-type and on the single vs double variant switch, so it
shows a blank draft each time. The typed draft lives in Rust state and
survives hide/show, so to mirror native we clear the input draft on this
hide transition ONLY.

calls this ONLY when the hide is an in-container order-type / variant
switch (`!isHiddenByAncestor()`); a Home / Trade tab switch hides the
shell too, so it does NOT call this and the draft is PRESERVED (native
keeps the cache slot on tab-return). Sibling parity with
`PureSpotLimitInteractor::on_hidden`.

side switch / pair switch / logout edge (`apply_side_state_mutation`
side_changed block + `reset_for_logout`): trigger price, order price,
amount, seekbar. Additive action, forward-compatible with bindings that
never call it.

variants.name: SubmitErrorToast
variants.doc:
Transient toast bridge for `LeverageBusinessError::GeneralError` —
the only error variant whose behavior strategy is `Toast`. The
persistent rendering still flows through state (input section error
/ submit error_message); this event triggers the additional
transient toast. `message` is a CDKey-resolvable string.

variants.name: HighLeverageConfirmationRequired
variants.doc:
The facade requires the user to confirm a high-leverage submission.
Native renders the warning dialog using the provided CDKeys and bolds
the leverage number(s) carried by `long_trigger` / `short_trigger`.
Native calls `confirm_high_leverage_warning(section_id)` to continue
or `cancel_high_leverage_confirmation()` to abort.

Exactly one of `long_trigger` / `short_trigger` is `Some` for the
dual single-side cases; both are `Some` when long+short both trip.
For single / margin scenarios `long_trigger` carries the section id
(`"single"` / `"margin"`) and `short_trigger` is `None`.

variants.name: SubmitAccountRiskSuccess
variants.doc:
AccountRiskComparison scenario-specific success variant. Carries the
full BE `SwitchAccountPresetResponse` so callers (e.g.
`RiskComparisonBottomDialog`) can read `lever` / `curAcctLv` /
`acctLv` / `riskOffsetType` and decide their own dismiss + toast
behavior. The S16 contract diverges from the other 6 scenarios:
V2 must NOT self-toast or self-dismiss here. The other scenarios
continue to use `SubmitFullSuccess` (which Native interprets as
"show success toast + dismiss page").

variants.name: SubmitAccountRiskError
variants.doc:
AccountRiskComparison scenario-specific failure variant. Paired with
`SubmitAccountRiskSuccess` so V1 callers always receive a
`(success, resp)` signal (V1
`AccountRiskCompAdjustLeverDFragment.kt:115-116` invokes
`mSubmitCallback?.invoke(false, null)` on failure). Native still
renders the persistent error through state (R2 red line — error
message stays in `page_vo.error`), but this transient signals the
caller's callback fire.

doc:
One-shot UI events emitted to native after each action completes.

UxEvent (one branch = one variant) rule: never reuse a variant with a
"kind" tag. See `spec/interactor.md` §F.

All user-visible strings are CDKeys (per §D + §F) — Rust does not know
the device locale and never hardcodes natural language.

**Phase 5.1 contract**: submit outcomes are split into three transient
events plus a state-only "all failed" channel. Errors are not routed
through a generic `SubmitError` variant — `mapper::apply_submit_error`
reflects them onto `page_vo.is_locked` / `submit.error_message` /
`input_sections[*].error` (R2 red line: errors do not ride on transient
toasts), and only `LeverageBusinessError::GeneralError` additionally
surfaces `SubmitErrorToast` as a transient bridge (the persistent
rendering still flows through state — see `mapper::apply_submit_error`).
